The chart in Q2 is given as text (its official version for visually impaired candidates), and Q5(A) uses its official text version. Model answers are written for this portal and are not CBSE's official marking scheme.

questions.subject: English
questions.text:
Read the text given below :
(1) Held every year on 21 May, UNESCO leads the celebration of World Day for Cultural Diversity for Dialogue and Development highlighting not only the richness of the world's cultures, but also the essential role of intercultural dialogue for achieving peace and sustainable development.
(2) A recent international emergency has proved the intrinsic value of the cultural and creative sector at generating social cohesion, educational resource or personal well-being in times of crisis. It has also underscored the sector's potential to generate economic growth, something which is too often underestimated.
(3) With the adoption in September 2015 of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development by the United Nations, and the resolution on Culture and Sustainable Development adopted by the UN General Assembly in December 2015, the message of the World Day for Cultural Diversity for Dialogue and Development is more important than ever. The 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) can best be achieved by drawing upon the creative potential of the world's diverse cultures and engaging in continuous dialogue to ensure that all members of society benefit from sustainable development.
(4) Bridging the gap between cultures is urgent and necessary for peace, stability and development. Cultural diversity is a driving force of development, not only with respect to economic growth, but also as a means of leading a more fulfilling intellectual, emotional, moral and spiritual life. This is captured in the culture conventions, which provide a solid basis for the promotion of cultural diversity. Cultural diversity is thus an asset that is indispensable for poverty reduction and the achievement of sustainable development.
(5) At the same time, acceptance and recognition of cultural diversity in particular through innovative use of media and Information and Communications Technologies (ICTs) are conducive to dialogue among civilizations and cultures, respect and mutual understanding.
(6) In 2001, UNESCO adopted the Universal Declaration on Cultural Diversity. Next, in December 2002, the UN General Assembly, in its resolution 57/249, declared May 21 to be the World Day for Cultural Diversity for Dialogue and Development, and in 2015, the Second Committee of the UN General Assembly unanimously adopted the resolution on Culture and Sustainable Development, affirming culture's contribution to the three dimensions of sustainable development, acknowledging further the natural and cultural diversity of the world, and recognizing that cultures and civilizations can contribute to, and are crucial enablers of, sustainable development.
(7) The day provides us with an opportunity to deepen our understanding of the values of cultural diversity and to achieve the goals of the UNESCO Convention on the Protection and Promotion of the Diversity of Cultural Expressions adopted on 20 October, 2005.

Answer the following questions :
(i) List 2 points to describe the purpose of UNESCO leading the celebration of World Day for Cultural Diversity for Dialogue and Development. (1)
(ii) Select the option that corresponds to the meaning of : 'The recent international emergency has proved the intrinsic value of the cultural and creative sector at generating social cohesion, educational resource or personal well-being in times of crisis.' (A) the real worth of cultural sector at generating social cohesion during pandemics (B) the real worth of creative sector at undermining the social cohesion during an international emergency (C) questioning the real worth of creative sector at generating education resource during an international emergency (D) highlighting the real worth of cultural and creative sector at generating social cohesion and educational resource during an international emergency (1)
(iii) Examine in about 40 words how Sustainable Development Goals can be achieved. (2)
(iv) What is the tone of the writer in the line "Cultural diversity is an asset." ? Rationalise your response in about 40 words. (2)
(v) The phrase 'bridging the gap' in paragraph (4) refers to : (A) widening the differences (B) connecting two disparate ideas (C) supporting the bridging (D) filling in the space between two connected things (1)
(vi) In sets a–e, identify two sets of synonyms : a. richness and poverty b. intellectual and moral c. reduction and promotion d. essential and intrinsic e. urgent and crucial. (A) a and c (B) b and e (C) d and e (D) b and d (1)
(vii) Complete : The Second Committee of UN General Assembly in 2015 adopted ______. (1)
(viii) Complete : ______ is urgent and necessary for peace, stability and development. (1)
questions.solution: (i) (a) To highlight the richness of the world's cultures. (b) To stress the role of intercultural dialogue in achieving peace and sustainable development. (ii) (D). (iii) By drawing on the creative potential of the world's diverse cultures and engaging in continuous dialogue, so that all members of society benefit from sustainable development. (iv) Positive/appreciative: the writer values cultural diversity as a driving force of development and an indispensable asset for poverty reduction and a fulfilling intellectual, emotional, moral and spiritual life. (v) (B). (vi) (C) d and e. (vii) the resolution on Culture and Sustainable Development. (viii) Bridging the gap between cultures.

questions.subject: English
questions.text:
Read the extract given below :
(1) The National Education Policy 2020 proposes the revision and revamping of all aspects of education, including the educational structure, regulations and governance, to create a new system which is aligned with the aspirational goals of 21st century students. According to the policy, by 2025, at least 50% of learners through the school and higher education system shall have exposure to skill education, for which a clear action plan with targets and timelines are to be developed.
(2) The policy aims to overcome the social status hierarchy associated with skill education and integration of skill education into mainstream education in all educational institutions in a phased manner. Beginning with skill exposure at early ages in middle and secondary school, quality skill education will be integrated smoothly into school and higher education.
(3) Every child will learn at least one skill and is exposed to several more. This would lead to emphasizing the dignity of labour and importance of various vocations involving Indian arts and artisanship.
(4) The development of skill capacities will go hand-in-hand with the development of 'academic' or other capacities. To achieve this objective, secondary schools will have to collaborate with Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs), Polytechnics, Local Industry, etc. Skill labs will also be set up and created in the schools in a Hub and Spoke model, which will allow other schools to use the facility. Higher education institutions will offer skill education either on their own or in partnership with industry and other institutions.
The Global Scenario of Students in Skill Education (percentage of students in skill education) : India 5%, Egypt 30%, Denmark 50%, USA 52%, Germany 75%, South Korea 96%.

Answer the questions :
(i) List 2 objectives of NEP 2020. (2)
(ii) Fill in the blanks : "The development of skill capacities will go hand-in-hand with the development of academic or other capacities" is a/an ______ (fact/opinion) because it is a/an ______ (subjective judgement/objective detail). (1)
(iii) "According to the policy, by 2025, at least 50% of learners through the school and higher education system shall have exposure to skill education." This means : (A) Maximum 50% learners shall have exposure to technical education. (B) Minimum 50% learners shall have exposure to technical education. (C) Minimum 50% learners shall have exposure to skill education. (D) Maximum 50% learners shall have exposure to skill education. (1)
(iv) Complete : The benefit of the hub and spoke model will be ______. (1)
(v) Complete the analogy with a word/phrase from paragraph (3) : Racism : condemn :: ______ : respect (1)
(vi) As per the Global Scenario, which country has the maximum percentage of students in skill education and what can be the possible reason ? (2)
(vii) As per NEP 2020, skill exposure will begin at : (A) middle and secondary school (B) primary school (C) higher school (D) senior secondary school (1)
(viii) Justify the statement : 'The NEP will create an awareness and appreciation of Indian arts and artisanship.' (1)
questions.solution: (i) Any two: revamp all aspects of education to meet 21st-century aspirations; give at least 50% of learners exposure to skill education by 2025; remove the social status hierarchy attached to skill education; integrate skill education into mainstream education. (ii) fact; objective detail (it states a planned policy measure). (iii) (C). (iv) that other schools can use the skill labs set up in one school (shared facilities). (v) dignity of labour. (vi) South Korea (96%). A possible reason: skill education is integrated into its mainstream schooling and valued by society, with strong links to industry. (vii) (A). (viii) Every child will learn at least one skill and be exposed to several more, which emphasises the dignity of labour and the importance of vocations involving Indian arts and artisanship.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Fill in the blank using the correct form of the word in brackets, for the given portion of a letter : Dear Sir, In response to your query, the document that ______ (explain) our country's sustainability initiatives has been attached for your consideration.
questions.solution: explains

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Identify the error and supply the correction : The uniquely flavoured dish was interestingly enough to captivate my taste buds.
questions.solution: Error: interestingly. Correction: interesting.

questions.subject: English
questions.text:
Raashi and Ratul had a conversation about volunteer work. Report Raashi's question.
Raashi : What challenges have you faced while volunteering ?
Ratul : The main challenge is dealing with different personalities, but it's also a great learning experience.
questions.solution: Raashi asked Ratul what challenges he had faced while volunteering.

questions.subject: English
questions.text:
Librarian : Welcome back! It's good to see you, young man!
Student : Thanks! I was overloaded with assignments, so I have not visited the library this week.
The librarian greeted the student warmly, expressing pleasure at his visit. The student thanked her and explained that ______ which had limited his recent visits to the library.
options: he had been overloaded with assignments
he has been overloaded with assignments
questions.solution: In reported speech the simple past 'was' moves back to the past perfect 'had been'.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Fill in the blank : The revised meeting agenda is attached and ______ needs to be emailed to all participants before the meeting.
questions.solution: 'It' refers back to the agenda already mentioned.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Identify the error and supply the correction for the sentence from an e-commerce website's return policy : We offers a 30-day return policy on all unopened products purchased from our websites.
questions.solution: Error: offers. Correction: offer. (Also accepted: 'websites' → 'website'.)

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for the sentence from a public health campaign : The campaign's goal is to increase physical activity among the younger.
questions.solution: 'The younger' needs a noun; 'among the youth' is correct.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Complete the narrative : The internship at the tech startup had me ______ excited about the potential of innovation and entrepreneurial spirit.
questions.solution: 'Had me feeling' (have + object + -ing) describes the effect the internship had.

questions.subject: English
questions.text:
Vendor : You look a little different today! Customer : Yes, I just got a new haircut.
The vendor noticed that his customer's appearance had changed and asked him about it. The customer admitted this, citing the fact that ______.
questions.solution: he had just got a new haircut.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Complete the update on the regional science fair : We have exciting news to share! Our school ______ first place in the regional science fair.
questions.solution: A recent result being announced now takes the present perfect passive 'has been awarded'.

questions.subject: English
questions.text:
Complete the line from a song :
The morning dew captures your essence,
The flowers and grass ______ your colour,
The Sunrise embraces your arrival,
As the dawn welcomes a new day.
questions.solution: The plural subject 'the flowers and grass' takes 'reflect', matching the present tense of the other lines.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Identify the error and supply the correction : The public health campaign aimed in increase awareness of the risks associated with underage drinking.
questions.solution: Error: in increase. Correction: to increase (or 'at increasing').

questions.subject: English
questions.text: There are daily reports in the newspaper of fatal accidents due to reckless driving and road rage. Write a letter to the Commissioner of Traffic Police in about 120 words suggesting the need to take stricter action against the offenders. Recommend the use of social media to launch awareness campaigns about the implications of irresponsible driving. You are Shantanu / Savita, living at B-108 Krishi Apartments.
questions.solution: Format (1 mark): sender's address, date, The Commissioner of Traffic Police, subject (Need for strict action against reckless driving), salutation, close, name. Content (2 marks): rising fatal accidents from speeding, drunk driving, jumping signals and road rage; suggestions: heavy fines, licence suspension, more CCTV and speed cameras, regular checking; social-media campaigns with short videos, real stories, influencers and hashtags to show the consequences of irresponsible driving; request for prompt action. Organisation and accuracy (2 marks).

questions.subject: English
questions.text: A leading communication company 'Savera' is sponsoring a half marathon run in your city to raise funds for 'Koshish' an orphanage. You are Roshini/Roshan, school captain of Adarsh Vidyalaya. You are leading a batch of hundred students in the half marathon to be held in your city. Write a letter to the editor of a national daily emphasizing the participation of school children in such programmes as part of voluntary community service. Highlight the benefits of participation in such activities.
questions.solution: Format (1 mark): sender's address, date, The Editor and newspaper, subject (School students and community service through charity events), salutation, close, name and designation. Content (2 marks): the Savera half marathon for the Koshish orphanage; a hundred students of Adarsh Vidyalaya taking part; such events teach empathy, social responsibility, teamwork and discipline; they promote fitness and confidence; they connect schools with the community; an appeal to schools and parents to encourage participation. Organisation and accuracy (2 marks).

questions.subject: English
questions.text: The following are notes about the four stages in the metamorphosis of butterflies. Summarise the notes in the form of an analytical paragraph : Eggs → larva (known as caterpillar) → pupa (known as chrysalis) → adult (known as butterfly).
questions.solution: Introduction: a butterfly's life cycle has four distinct stages (complete metamorphosis). Analysis: the female lays eggs on leaves; each egg hatches into a larva, or caterpillar, whose main job is to eat and grow; the caterpillar then forms a pupa, or chrysalis, a resting stage in which its body is completely rebuilt; finally an adult butterfly emerges, able to fly and reproduce, and the cycle begins again. Comparison and conclusion: the caterpillar and butterfly look completely different, showing a remarkable transformation. Marks: content 3, accuracy 2.

questions.subject: English
questions.text:
Study the table which shows the data on the hobbies of students during summer vacations. Write an analytical paragraph in about 120 words analyzing what hobbies boys and girls choose in their summer vacations.
Hobbies : Boys / Girls
Singing : 7% / 25%
Photography : 35% / 5%
Playing : 30% / 16%
Dancing : 13% / 40%
Yoga : 19% / 15%
questions.solution: Introduction: the table compares the summer hobbies of boys and girls. Analysis: boys most prefer photography (35%) and playing (30%), while very few girls choose photography (5%). Girls most prefer dancing (40%) and singing (25%), whereas only 13% and 7% of boys choose these. Yoga is the most evenly liked hobby (boys 19%, girls 15%). Conclusion: boys lean towards outdoor and technical hobbies and girls towards performing arts, though yoga appeals to both. Marks: content 3, accuracy 2.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: First Flight: Nelson Mandela – Long Walk to Freedom
questions.text:
Read the extract and answer the questions :
On the day of the inauguration, I was overwhelmed with a sense of history. In the first decade of the 20th century a few years after the bitter Anglo-Boer war and before my own birth, the white skinned people of South Africa patched up their differences and created a system of racial domination against the dark-skinned people of their own land. The structure they created formed the basis of one of the harshest, most inhumane societies the world has ever known. Now, in the last decade of the twentieth century, and my own eighth decade as a man, that system has been overturned forever and replaced by one that recognised the rights and freedoms of all peoples, regardless of the colour of their skin.
(i) Explain the feelings of the narrator when he said, "I was overwhelmed with a sense of history." (1)
(ii) The system of racial domination has been replaced by a system that : (A) confirms the education of the Blacks (B) recognises the rights and freedoms of all people (C) recollects the bitter experiences (D) focuses on the personality development (1)
(iii) Comment on the kind of society apartheid had created. (2)
(iv) Which phrase would correctly substitute 'patched up' in : "...the white skinned people of South Africa patched up their differences..." (1)
questions.solution: (i) He felt deeply moved and proud, recalling the long history of racial oppression and the struggle that had led to this historic moment of freedom. (ii) (B). (iii) Apartheid created one of the harshest, most inhumane societies ever known, in which white people dominated the dark-skinned people of their own land, denying them rights, freedom and dignity. (iv) settled / resolved / made up.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: First Flight: From the Diary of Anne Frank
questions.text:
Read the extract and answer the questions :
I started right away at the Montessori Nursery School. I stayed there until I was six, at which time I started in the first form. In the sixth form, my teacher was Mrs. Kuperus, the headmistress. At the end of the year we were both in tears as we said a heartbreaking farewell. In the summer of 1941, Grandma fell ill and had to have an operation, so my birthday passed with little celebration.
(i) "In the summer of 1941, Grandma fell ill and had to have an operation, so my birthday passed with little celebration." State any one inference about Anne from this. (1)
(ii) The first education of Anne started at : (A) some Kindergarten School (B) a Nursery School (C) Montessori Nursery School (D) Elementary School (1)
(iii) Who was Mrs. Kuperus ? What kind of relationship did Anne share with her ? (2)
(iv) Substitute the word 'heartbreaking' with a word similar in meaning : "At the end of the year we were both in tears as we said a heartbreaking farewell." (1)
questions.solution: (i) Anne was sensitive and caring; she loved her grandmother and put her well-being above her own celebration. (ii) (C). (iii) Mrs Kuperus was the headmistress and Anne's teacher in the sixth form. They shared a close, affectionate bond; both were in tears when they said goodbye. (iv) painful / sorrowful / tearful.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: First Flight: A Tiger in the Zoo
questions.text:
Read the extract and answer the questions :
He stalks in his vivid stripes
The few steps of his cage,
On pads of velvet quiet,
In his quiet rage.
He should be lurking in shadow,
Sliding through long grass
Near the water hole
Where plump deer pass.
He should be snarling around houses
At the jungle's edge,
Baring his white fangs, his claws,
Terrorising the village!
(i) State any one point of contrast between the tiger in the zoo and in its natural habitat. (1)
(ii) When the speaker suggests that the tiger should be "snarling around houses at the jungle's edge", what does he insinuate about the tiger's natural behaviour and habitat ? (1)
(iii) The poet's skilful use of imagery effectively depicts the confinement and frustration of the tiger. Elaborate in about 40 words. (2)
(iv) Which phrase would correctly substitute 'quiet rage' in the line ? (1)
questions.solution: (i) In the zoo it paces a few steps in a small cage; in the wild it would lurk in shadows and hunt freely near a water hole. (ii) That the tiger is naturally wild, powerful and fearsome, and belongs in the forest where it can roam and assert itself. (iii) 'The few steps of his cage' shows how cramped he is; 'quiet rage' shows anger he cannot express; images of lurking in long grass and baring fangs contrast his lost freedom with his helpless captivity. (iv) silent anger / suppressed fury.

questions.subject: English
questions.text:
Read the extract and answer the questions :
No use to say 'O there are other balls'
An ultimate shaking grief fixes the boy
As he stands rigid, trembling, staring down
All his young days into the harbour where his ball went.
I would not intrude on him,
A dime, another ball, is worthless. Now
He senses first responsibility
In a world of possessions. People will take
Balls, balls will be lost always, little boy
And no one buys a ball back. Money is external
He is learning.....
(i) Which best describes the speaker's attitude towards the boy's reaction to losing his ball ? (A) indifferent as the ball is inexpensive (B) sympathetic, understanding the depth of the boy's loss (C) mocking, finding the boy's reaction exaggerated and unnecessary (D) panicked, sharing the boy's distress over the lost ball (1)
(ii) Comment on the use of metaphor in the above extract. (1)
(iii) Explain the phrase 'all his young days into the harbour' with reference to the extract. (1)
(iv) Briefly state in about 40 words the boy's journey from 'shaking grief' to 'he is learning'. (2)
questions.solution: (i) (B). (ii) The ball is a metaphor for the things we lose in life (childhood, possessions, loved ones); its loss stands for the first experience of loss. (iii) The boy stares at the water where his ball fell, and with it the happy memories of his childhood seem to sink too. (iv) At first the boy is shaken and frozen with grief. The poet does not console him, so he learns on his own that losses happen, money cannot buy them back, and he must bear them; this is his first step towards maturity.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: What mood of the poet is reflected in the poem 'Dust of Snow' initially ? What images are used by the poet to bring about the effect ? Comment. Answer in 40–50 words.
questions.solution: At first the poet is sad and depressed, regretting the day. Frost uses the crow (often a sign of bad omen) and the hemlock tree (poisonous) to reflect this gloom. Ironically, the crow shaking snow dust from the hemlock lifts his mood and saves part of the day.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: How far would you agree that one's positivity can bring in a spark of brightness even in adverse circumstances ? Answer in 40–50 words.
questions.solution: I fully agree. In 'A Letter to God', Lencho's faith gave him hope after the hailstorm destroyed his crop; in 'Dust of Snow', a small natural act changed the poet's gloomy mood. A positive outlook helps us see opportunities and keep going, turning even difficult moments into hope.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: First Flight: The Tale of Custard the Dragon
questions.text: What makes Custard, the dragon look fearsome ? Explain. Answer in 40–50 words.
questions.solution: Custard had big sharp teeth and spikes on top of him and scales underneath; his mouth was like a fireplace, his nose like a chimney and his toes like daggers. These features made him look fearsome, though ironically he was considered a coward until he fought the pirate.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Explain why the speaker mentions God in the poem "For Anne Gregory". Answer in 40–50 words.
questions.solution: The speaker says that people, especially young men, love Anne for her beautiful yellow hair, i.e. her outward beauty. He mentions God because only God can love a person for themselves alone, for their inner self, not for appearance. Human love is shaped by looks, while divine love is unconditional.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: First Flight: The Sermon at Benares
questions.text: What message might the Buddha's story hold for those who are in positions of power and privilege ? Answer in 40–50 words.
questions.solution: Prince Siddhartha left his luxurious life after seeing sickness, old age and death, realising that power and wealth cannot protect anyone from suffering. The message is that privilege is temporary; the powerful should be humble, compassionate and seek true wisdom, using their position to reduce others' suffering.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: Footprints without Feet: Footprints without Feet
questions.text: Scientists contribute to make the world a better place. Griffin is an antithesis to this statement. Justify. (Footprints Without Feet) Answer in 40–50 words.
questions.solution: Griffin was a brilliant scientist who discovered how to become invisible, but he used it for selfish, criminal ends. He set fire to his landlord's house, robbed a shop and a clergyman's home, and attacked people at the inn. Instead of benefiting humanity, he became a lawless menace.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why did Bholi's teacher feel like an artist admiring her masterpiece ? (Bholi) Answer in 40–50 words.
questions.solution: With kindness and encouragement, the teacher turned Bholi, a timid, stammering girl ignored by her family, into a confident, educated young woman who stood up against Bishamber's greed. Seeing this transformation she had shaped, the teacher felt like an artist admiring her finished masterpiece.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: What is the twist at the end of the story 'The Necklace' ? (The Necklace) Answer in 40–50 words.
questions.solution: After ten years of poverty and hard work spent repaying the debt for a replacement diamond necklace, Matilda meets Mme Forestier and tells her the truth. Mme Forestier reveals that the original necklace was fake, worth at most five hundred francs. Their sacrifice was all for nothing.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: First Flight: A Baker from Goa / Nelson Mandela
questions.text: In the chapter 'A Baker from Goa' the narrator talks about his childhood in Goa and his fond memories. In about 120 words write a presentation draft comparing the childhood of the narrator in 'A Baker from Goa' to that of Nelson Mandela. You may begin this way : Childhood memories remind us of the days gone by.....
questions.solution: Childhood memories remind us of the days gone by. The narrator of 'A Baker from Goa' recalls a carefree, joyful childhood: waiting eagerly for the baker's jingling bamboo staff each morning, rushing to get bread bangles and sweet loaves, and the baker's role in festivals and weddings. His memories are of simple pleasures in a close-knit community. Nelson Mandela's childhood was also free at first: he ran in the fields near his mother's hut, swam in streams and roasted mealies. But as he grew up he realised that, as a black boy, his freedom was an illusion, restricted by apartheid laws. While the narrator's childhood stayed innocent and happy, Mandela's led him to a lifelong struggle for freedom.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: First Flight: Amanda! / From the Diary of Anne Frank
questions.text: Amanda from the poem 'Amanda' is a teenager like Anne Frank and lives in her fantasy world whereas Anne is a chatter box. What conversation will Anne Frank have with Amanda about different perspectives of life ? Write your answer in about 120 words.
questions.solution: A good answer is a dialogue. Anne: Amanda, you look lost in thought. Amanda: I'm tired of being told what to do: sit straight, don't eat chocolates, do your homework. I'd rather be a mermaid on a calm sea. Anne: I understand. My teacher punished me for talking too much, but I wrote an essay, 'A Chatterbox', and turned it into a joke. Amanda: You didn't get angry? Anne: Expressing yourself helps. I keep a diary, Kitty, and pour out my feelings. Dreams are lovely, but sharing your feelings and using humour can change things. Amanda: Maybe I should talk to my mother instead of escaping. Anne: Yes, and keep a diary too. The answer should show Amanda's escapism and Anne's expressiveness. Marks: content 3, expression 3.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: Footprints without Feet: A Question of Trust
questions.text: How did the lady in red manage to outsmart and out manoeuvre the other thief, Horace Danby, by robbing the safe without leaving a single fingerprint ? (A Question of Trust) Answer in 100–120 words.
questions.solution: When Horace Danby broke into Shotover Grange, a young woman in red appeared and calmly posed as the lady of the house. She did not call the police; instead she flattered him and said she had forgotten the combination of the safe and needed her jewels for a party. Trusting her, Horace opened the safe for her without gloves, after his sneezing (hay fever) made him use his handkerchief. She wore gloves throughout, took the jewels and left. When the jewels were reported stolen, the police found only Horace's fingerprints, and he was arrested. Her cleverness, composure and acting outwitted the careful thief.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: Footprints without Feet: The Thief's Story
questions.text: Hari Singh says – "He knew it but neither his lips nor his eyes showed anything." Anil successfully addressed the situation by not addressing it at all. Elaborate based on your reading of The Thief's Story. Answer in 100–120 words.
questions.solution: Hari Singh, a young thief, stole Anil's six hundred rupees and ran to catch a train, but changed his mind, realising he would lose the chance to be educated and trusted. He returned and put the money back under the mattress. In the morning Anil gave him a fifty-rupee note, which was still damp from the night's rain, so Hari knew Anil had discovered the theft. Yet Anil said nothing and promised to teach him to write sentences. By staying silent, Anil showed forgiveness and trust, preserved Hari's dignity and gave him a chance to reform. This silent kindness changed Hari more than punishment ever could.
